title: Real-time global pathogen surveillance and data sharing
bottleneck: Outbreak detection depends on fragmented national systems, and many countries lack genomic sequencing or real-time reporting; sovereignty concerns and commercial interests further slow sharing of pathogen data. The result is weeks-to-months delays between spillover and global awareness.
why_it_blocks: Every pandemic plan assumes early warning, but the warning system itself is the weakest link. Without rapid, transparent surveillance, vaccines and countermeasures always start behind the pathogen.
current_state: WHO's pandemic agreement negotiations include a Pathogen Access and Benefit-Sharing system, but ratification is pending. Genomic surveillance expanded after COVID-19 yet remains concentrated in wealthy countries. Wastewater and metagenomic sequencing can detect novel pathogens without clinical cases, but global coverage is patchy and data-sharing norms during outbreaks remain voluntary and slow.
